### Discovery & Translational Science

* **Analysis reveals target convergence and delivery challenges across RNA therapeutic pipeline** [Andrew Pannu on X](https://x.com/andrewpannu/status/2102763696812413129)
  * An industry report analyzing over 3,100 therapeutic oligonucleotide programs indicates that liver-directed RNA drugs are transitioning into a product execution phase, whereas extrahepatic targeting remains primarily a delivery hurdle.
  * GalNAc-mediated delivery enabled eight RNA drug approvals for Alnylam and Ionis between 2019 and 2025, but standardized sequence design and chemical modifications have resulted in heavy target convergence across competitive pipelines.
  * GalNAc conjugate patents are scheduled to begin expiring in 2028, which is anticipated to intensify market competition within liver-expressed targets.
* **Embryonic dual origin of the brain**
  * A study in *Nature Neuroscience* suggests the mammalian brain develops as a composite organ rather than a single unified structure.
  * The research focuses on the distinct, earliest embryonic origins of the forebrain compared to the midbrain and hindbrain, challenging classical models of continuous neural tube development.
* **AI-assisted design of biological weapons** [Science](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/ai-help-biological-or-chemical-weapons)
  * Anthropic reported implementing safeguards within its Claude AI systems to block queries aimed at modifying viruses—specifically chikungunya, avian influenza, and an undisclosed orthopoxvirus.
  * The report has drawn mixed reviews from experts, with debate over whether the queries represented genuine bioweapon design attempts or routine academic and virology inquiries.
* **Progress in synthesizing carbyne-like structures** [Science](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/close-carbyne-we-re-probably-going-get)
  * A multicenter preprint details progress in synthesizing carbyne, a highly unstable, hypothetical carbon allotrope consisting of repeating carbon-carbon triple bonds.
  * To prevent the highly exothermic crosslinking reactions that destabilize long carbon chains, researchers are isolating and growing extended carbyne chains inside carbon nanotubes.
* **CircKif26b rescues age-related impaired angiogenesis** [npj Aging](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41514-026-00506-2)
  * Preclinical research shows that restoring the circular RNA CircKif26b rescues age-related impairment of angiogenesis.
  * The mechanism involves the stabilization of MOB4 and subsequent suppression of the Hippo signaling pathway.
* **Perspective on sex-biased mechanisms in cardiovascular medicine** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04659-1)
  * A perspective calls for redesigning cardiovascular research and medicine to integrate preclinical and clinical sex differences.
  * The authors emphasize the need to understand sex-biased molecular mechanisms, particularly in female-predominant cardiovascular conditions.
* **PTPN22 delayed negative feedback loop identified** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786963/)
  * A study demonstrates that the tyrosine phosphatase PTPN22 mediates delayed negative feedback of T cell activation.
  * PTPN22 exerts this inhibitory control by assembling a distinct signaling complex.
* **tRNA-gated cyclodepsipeptide pathway disarms bacterial development** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786558/)
  * Researchers characterized a tRNA-gated cyclodepsipeptide biosynthetic pathway that produces a chemical effector capable of disrupting bacterial development.
* **Pathophysiology of Yao syndrome** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786248/)
  * Multi-omics characterization of the autoinflammatory disorder Yao syndrome has mapped three distinct pathophysiological axes.
  * The findings highlight disease-specific divergence in molecular signaling between Yao syndrome and Blau syndrome.
* **Preclinical platform for antifibrotic compound screening** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786241/)
  * A paper introduces new approach methodologies establishing a drug screening platform to identify novel antifibrotic compounds.
* **Investigating weight loss resistance to GLP-1 drugs** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786216/)
  * Scientists are actively investigating the biological mechanisms explaining why a subset of patients fails to lose weight on GLP-1 receptor agonists.

### Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **Kyverna cell therapy shows sustained benefit in autoimmune disease** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/24/biotech-news-kyverna-cell-therapy-shows-lasting-autoimmune-benefit/)
  * Kyverna Therapeutics reported updated clinical data for its lead CAR-T cell therapy, demonstrating long-term clinical efficacy in autoimmune disease.
  * A significant portion of treated patients remained entirely off of standard immunosuppressive or disease-modifying therapies during follow-up.
* **[Biotech]** **Kyverna reports durable one-year responses for miv-cel in SPS and gMG** [BioStocks on X](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103062317323735118)
  * Unconfirmed social media reports indicate Kyverna Therapeutics released positive one-year follow-up data for miv-cel in Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS) and generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).
  * The therapy demonstrated durable clinical efficacy and maintained a favorable safety profile at one year in both autoimmune indications.
* **[Biotech]** **Evorpacept combination improves ORR in HER2-positive gastric cancer** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04700-3)
  * Phase 2 results from the ASPEN-06 trial evaluated the next-generation CD47 blocker evorpacept in combination with trastuzumab, ramucirumab, and paclitaxel (TRP) in patients with advanced HER2-positive gastric cancer who progressed on prior anti-HER2 therapy.
  * Adding evorpacept to TRP led to a higher objective response rate (ORR) compared to TRP alone, with clinical responses correlating with baseline CD47 and HER2 expression levels.
* **[Biotech]** **Absci outlines Phase 2 trial of AI-designed antibody ABS-201** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103092581706191188)
  * Absci announced preliminary design details for its Phase 2 STORYLINE clinical trial of ABS-201.
  * ABS-201 is an AI-designed antibody being developed as a potential therapeutic for endometriosis.
* **[Big Pharma]** **Enpatoran shows pharmacodynamic activity in lupus despite missing Phase 2 primary endpoint** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01427-3/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Correspondence discussing Cohort B of the WILLOW trial for Merck KGaA's TLR7/8 inhibitor enpatoran in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) clarified that while the drug missed its primary dose-response analysis using the BICLA composite endpoint (p = 0.14), clinical responses suggested target engagement.
  * Patients achieved BICLA response rates of 49% to 58% across active treatment arms compared to 39% in the placebo group, pointing to a potential pharmacodynamic plateau rather than a total lack of efficacy.
* **High-dose NMN supplementation safely elevates NAD⁺ over 24 weeks** [npj Aging](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41514-026-00482-7)
  * A 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in older adults demonstrated that high-dose nicotinamide mononomucleotide (NMN) supplementation achieved sustained NAD⁺ augmentation.
* **Optimizing therapeutic index of peptide receptor radionuclide therapy** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42785954/)
  * A clinical study details the optimization of the therapeutic index of peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) utilizing sequential intraarterial-intravenous administration and personalized volumetric-adjusted dosing.
* **Pharmacokinetic profile of pirtobrutinib in hematological cancers** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786239/)
  * A population pharmacokinetic analysis of the non-covalent BTK inhibitor pirtobrutinib was published, using data from patients with hematological malignancies enrolled in the Phase 1/2 BRUIN trial.

### Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Merck's remigromig succeeds in Phase 2b/3 DME study, but signals potential ocular risks** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/merck-remigromig-dme-study-results-eyebio/831234/) / [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103074012175953931)
  * Merck's remigromig (formerly Restoret)—a tri-specific Wnt pathway agonist acquired in the $1.3 billion buyout of EyeBio—met its primary endpoint in the pivotal Phase 2b/3 BRUNELLO trial.
  * The study demonstrated non-inferiority in best-corrected visual acuity in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME) compared to those receiving Roche's Lucentis (ranibizumab).
  * However, Merck noted higher rates of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, bleeding inside the eye (intraocular hemorrhage), and treatment discontinuations in the remigromig cohort, prompting further safety analyses.
* **[Big Pharma]** **Roche and Ionis RNA drug sefaxersen hits primary endpoint in Phase 3 kidney trial** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/roche-ionis-rna-study-iga-nephropathy/831152/)
  * Roche and Ionis Pharmaceuticals announced that their experimental antisense oligonucleotide sefaxersen succeeded in an interim check of a Phase 3 study in IgA nephropathy.
  * The trial achieved its primary endpoint, showing a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in proteinuria (urine protein levels) compared to placebo.
  * The companies plan to present detailed findings at an upcoming medical congress and will monitor participants for two years to assess long-term changes in kidney function.
* **[Biotech]** **MediciNova completes double-blind dosing in Phase 2b/3 ALS trial** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103062793054494971)
  * MediciNova completed the last patient, last visit in the double-blind portion of its Phase 2b/3 COMBAT-ALS trial evaluating MN-166 (ibudilast) for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
  * Topline clinical data from the trial are expected by the end of this year.
* **Denosumab sequential therapy shows three-year outcomes** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42786015/)
  * Researchers published three-year extension trial results of a randomized clinical trial evaluating the long-term clinical efficacy and safety of denosumab sequential therapy.

### Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves Lilly's once-weekly insulin Onswik for type 2 diabetes** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-once-weekly-insulin-type-2-diabetes-mellitus) / [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103073860426027136)
  * The FDA approved Eli Lilly’s Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa-gobe), a once-weekly long-acting insulin analog to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
  * The subcutaneous injection is administered weekly on the same day and is not indicated for type 1 diabetes due to an elevated risk of severe hypoglycemia. It becomes the second once-weekly insulin approved in the US.
* **[Biotech]** **FDA approves Elevar's lirafugratinib for FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-lirafugratinib-previously-treated-unresectable-locally-advanced-or-metastatic) / [X/Twitter](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2103079098193006647)
  * The FDA granted approval to Elevar Therapeutics' kinase inhibitor Lyrfigtu (lirafugratinib) for adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic FGFR2 fusion- or rearrangement-positive cholangiocarcinoma.
  * Approval was based on the single-arm REFOCUS trial in 116 FGFR inhibitor-naive patients, showing a substantial objective response rate (ORR) and sustained duration of response.
  * Industry observers highlighted competitive questions regarding how the approval impacts the FGFR-inhibitor portfolios of peers like Relay Therapeutics and Incyte.
* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves belzutifan plus lenvatinib combination for advanced ccRCC** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-belzutifan-combination-lenvatinib-advanced-renal-cell-carcinoma-clear-cell-component)
  * The FDA approved Merck & Co.'s Welireg (belzutifan) in combination with Eisai's Lenvima (lenvatinib) for adults with advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC).
  * The combination is approved for patients whose disease progressed on or after receiving a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor.
  * Approval was based on the Phase 3 LITESPARK-011 trial of 747 patients, which demonstrated superior efficacy for the combination compared to cabozantinib.
* **[Biotech]** **Grail's Galleri cancer screening blood test wins FDA advisory committee backing** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/grail-multicancer-detection-test-wins-fda-advisers-backing/831286/)
  * An FDA advisory panel voted 7-2 (with one abstention) that the clinical benefits of Grail’s Galleri multicancer detection blood test outweigh its risks.
  * The panel voted unanimously that the test is safe, but split 6-4 on its effectiveness, raising concerns regarding potential false positives/negatives and the risk of patients skipping guideline-recommended standard-of-care screenings.
* **[Biotech]** **aTyr aligns with FDA on Phase 3 efzofitimod protocol in pulmonary sarcoidosis** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103062587764261323)
  * aTyr Pharma announced that it has aligned with the FDA on the design and regulatory requirements of its upcoming Phase 3 trial of efzofitimod in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.
* **FDA nominee Heidi Overton parries questions during Senate hearing** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/overton-senate-hearing-fda-vaccines-abortion-china/831285/) / [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/24/heidi-overton-fda-commissioner-confirmation-hearing-2/)
  * Dr. Heidi Overton, nominee to head the FDA, testified before a Senate committee, pledging to make decisions on vaccines and the abortion drug mifepristone based strictly on legal and scientific frameworks if faced with political pressure.
  * Overton emphasized her priorities to accelerate early-stage drug development and streamline approval processes to maintain US competitiveness against China's fast-growing biotechnology industry.
* **FDA drafts labeling guidance on drug interactions and QTc interval prolongation** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/communicating-drug-interaction-and-qtc-information-us-prescribing-information-09232026)
  * The FDA hosted a workshop regarding its October 2024 draft guidance on formatting drug interaction and QTc interval prolongation warnings in human prescription drug labeling.
  * The guidance aims to standardize where and how clinically significant drug-drug interaction mechanisms and dose-modification warnings are communicated to prescribers.
* **Regulatory lessons from Compass Therapeutics' crossover clinical data** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2102731968173547755)
  * Industry analysts highlighted a cautionary FDA regulatory precedent for Compass Therapeutics, noting that the agency rejected patient crossover as a valid excuse for a lack of overall survival (OS) benefit when developers seek to move cancer therapies into earlier lines of treatment.
* **Streamlining platform gene therapy regulatory approvals** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/bradloncar/status/2102818504395395519)
  * Speaking at the OH Rare Disease Symposium 2026, gene editing pioneer Fyodor Urnov argued for streamlined manufacturing certifications for rare disease therapies, noting, "If you have a pizza place and you change the topping, you don't re-certify the oven."
* **User fee reauthorizations and impurity guidelines** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/industry/biosimilar-user-fee-amendments/bsufa-iv-fiscal-years-2028-2032) / [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/cder-nitrosamine-impurity-acceptable-intake-limits)
  * The FDA announced preparation for the fourth reauthorization of the Biosimilar User Fee Act (BsUFA IV, FY2028-2032) and is holding a public workshop on the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) reauthorization.
  * The agency also updated its guidance on CDER nitrosamine impurity limits, outlining acceptable intake levels for drug-substance-related impurities using predicted carcinogenic potency categorization models.

### Business & Strategy

* **[Biotech]** **ADARx prices $446M IPO, gains separate $89M investment from AbbVie** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/adarx-rnai-biotech-ipo-stock-pricing/831262/)
  * RNA interference (RNAi) specialist ADARx Pharmaceuticals priced its IPO at the top of its range at $17 per share, securing $446.3 million.
  * The biotech also raised $89 million in a concurrent private placement from its development partner AbbVie, providing capital to advance its pipeline designed to overcome historical delivery and potency challenges of RNA therapeutics.
* **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly inks $3.35B target discovery deal with Beijing's InnoCare Pharma** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lilly-innocare-immunovant-vertex-inaxaplin-otsuka-ionis/831044/)
  * Eli Lilly agreed to pay InnoCare Pharma $100 million upfront and up to $3.25 billion in milestone payments to discover and develop therapeutic compounds against up to five targets in cancer and autoimmune disease.
  * The deal represents Lilly’s fourth collaboration with a China-based biotech since the beginning of 2025.
* **[Biotech]** **Enveda Biosciences raises $311M Series E for clinical-stage programs** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/enveda-ai-drug-discovery-series-e/831161/)
  * Enveda Biosciences closed a $311 million Series E venture round to transition its AI-driven natural product drug-discovery platform into clinical development.
  * The company is currently screening 17 candidate programs and has three assets active in human clinical trials.
* **[Biotech]** **Immunovant halts anti-FcRn IMVT-1402 development in cutaneous lupus** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lilly-innocare-immunovant-vertex-inaxaplin-otsuka-ionis/831044/)
  * Immunovant and parent Roivant Sciences announced a clinical development halt for IMVT-1402 in cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) following an undisclosed trial setback.
* **[Biotech]** **Fate Therapeutics receives $15M grant for lupus nephritis trial** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2103439901874131163)
  * Fate Therapeutics secured a $15 million CLIN2 grant from the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine (CIRM).
  * The funding will directly support the clinical advancement of its RECLAIM-LN trial evaluating its cell therapy candidate in lupus nephritis.
* **Pharma board chairs warn of European R&D and clinical trial decline** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/europe-biotech-investment-decline-letter-pharma-chairs/831112/)
  * Nine European pharma board chairs published an open letter warning that Europe's share of global pharma R&D has dropped to 31% (down from 43% in 1990), while its share of clinical trials has halved to just 9%.
  * The leaders criticized policies that treat drugs as a government cost to suppress rather than an investment, warning that Europe is losing ground to international competition.
* **Indonesian high court rules against pharmaceutical patent evergreening** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/24/indonesian-court-rules-against-patent-evergreening-boosting-access-medicines/)
  * A court ruling in Indonesia has rejected several evergreening secondary patent filings by major pharmaceutical developers.
  * Patient advocates celebrated the verdict, calling it a template for developing countries seeking to lower generic drug barriers and improve local medicine access.
* **[Biotech]** **City Therapeutics files for initial public offering** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/bradloncar/status/2103269917332267270)
  * City Therapeutics, an emerging RNAi biotech co-founded by Alnylam veteran John Maraganore, has formally submitted its initial public offering registration.
* **Status of Kainova's EP4 antagonist clinical trial** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2103134939709685827)
  * Public databases reveal that Kainova’s clinical trial for its EP4 antagonist, DT-9081, has been terminated prematurely.
  * The company has had no public updates since April 2026, when it claimed clinical activity without providing data, raising questions regarding its current operating status.

### Public Health & Policy

* **Worst US measles outbreak since 1991 sees conflicting death counts** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/24/health-news-measles-contagious-outbreak-u-s-deaths-1991/) / [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/25/measles-deaths-statistics-pennsylvania-outbreak-cdc-nchs/) / [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/25/died-with-not-from-measles-physicians-explain-death-certificate-rules/)
  * The US is experiencing its most severe measles outbreak since 1991, with state officials in Pennsylvania reporting four deaths in unvaccinated individuals.
  * A clinical and political debate has emerged over "died with" versus "died of" designations on death certificates, which public health experts warn risks confusing the public about the actual lethality of the virus.
  * A discrepancy between federal CDC National Center for Health Statistics tracking and local state counters has further complicated the official death toll.
* **Big Tobacco used public comments to stall FDA menthol cigarette ban** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/25/fake-grassroots-campaign-jama-study-rutgers-researchers-fda-menthol-ban/)
  * A JAMA study published by Rutgers researchers shows that tobacco industry astroturfing campaigns flooded the FDA with over 175,000 public comments to delay a proposed 2022 menthol cigarette ban.
  * The vast majority of comments were identified as templated form letters repeating specific tobacco industry talking points.
* **Five candidates in the running to succeed WHO Director-General** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/25/world-health-organization-candidates-for-next-director-general/)
  * At least five candidates have emerged to campaign for the position of World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General.
  * The leadership transition occurs amidst heightening concerns regarding future US funding and global policy involvement.
* **ARPA-H launches Spectra initiative for lifespan autism research** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/25/russell-shilling-leads-arpa-h-spectra-initiative-autism-care/)
  * The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is planning a total-lifespan autism care project named the Spectra initiative, led by former military psychologist Russell Shilling.
* **HHS Deputy Secretary nominee Chris Klomp advanced by Senate Finance Committee** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/24/chris-klomp-vote-senate-finance-committee-hhs-deputy-secretary/)
  * The Senate Finance Committee voted to advance Chris Klomp to a full Senate vote to serve as the Deputy Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), positioning him as the primary operational deputy under department leadership.
* **State interest in Medicaid drug pricing program remains uncertain** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/24/trump-medicaid-generous-model-state-interest/)
  * Despite federal claims that all 50 states had expressed interest in participating in a new Medicaid drug pricing model, a survey of state agencies found that many remain undecided or are still evaluating the plan's feasibility.
* **Does expanding clinical trial capacity improve equitable healthcare access?** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04683-1)
  * An analysis of China's rapid clinical trial infrastructure expansion over the past decade indicates that trial capacity has concentrated in top-tier urban medical institutions.
  * The authors highlight that managing and decentralizing trial capacity is necessary to ensure equitable, nationwide patient access to innovative investigational drugs.

---

**Worth watching**
The safety signals emerging from Merck's Phase 2b/3 BRUNELLO trial of remigromig (higher rates of bleeding and proliferative retinopathy) will be heavily scrutinized by ophthalmology R&D leads to see if these represent target-mediated risks of systemic/local Wnt agonism or trial-specific patient selection issues.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Manipulating Vitamin D to fight Cancer! [New Research]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S8Ovpow0Ymo) -- Physionic
        - Clinical research evaluates the manipulation of the Vitamin D Receptor (VDR) to reprogram the tumor stroma, specifically targeting Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts (CAFs) to suppress pancreatitis and enhance pancreatic cancer therapy.
        - Multiple clinical trials have investigated the efficacy of combining the VDR agonist paricalcitol with standard chemotherapy regimens—such as gemcitabine, nab-paclitaxel, cisplatin, and 5-FU/LV—or immunotherapies like pembrolizumab for advanced or metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
        - Clinical data demonstrates a strong correlation between pre-treatment serum vitamin D deficiency and both increased systemic inflammatory biomarkers and significantly reduced overall survival rates in pancreatic cancer patients.
        - Active VDR signaling and vitamin D supplementation are being positioned as promising therapeutic adjuncts to standard-of-care chemoradiation therapy to improve patient prognosis.
    - [Today’s Tech Be Outdated in Just 6 Months?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/-stM4prPcoQ) -- Health2Tech
        - Ashley Cairns addresses the engineering and design challenge of building technology that remains relevant as artificial intelligence continues to evolve rapidly.
        - The discussion highlights strategies for tech startups and digital health companies to avoid creating solutions that face obsolescence within a six-to-twelve-month timeframe.
        - The focus is on designing adaptable systems that can integrate with future AI advancements rather than being replaced by them.
- Pure Science
    - [What happens when you open the valve?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/VKlulHwMxgU) -- Veritasium
        - The video presents a classic physics demonstration involving two balloons filled with unequal volumes of air.
        - The system is configured by connecting a highly inflated balloon and a minimally inflated balloon through a closed valve.
        - It poses a fundamental thermodynamic question regarding what occurs to the pressure and volume distribution between the two connected systems when the valve is opened.
- Other
    - [How Fast Can a Glacier Move: Crash Course Geology #19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OgYSITk0fSM) -- CrashCourse
        - The video examines the physical mechanisms of glacier formation, detailing how massive bodies of compacted ice accumulate and deform under their own weight.
        - It explores how glaciers dynamically sculpt the Earth's landscape by carving valleys, gouging out lake basins, and leaving distinct physical striations on bedrock.
        - Glaciers act as geologic archives that record historical climate data, allowing researchers to study past environmental conditions and analyze the future of ice sheets under contemporary climate shifts.
